newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar to tender 2,500T soyoil on April 30.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar to tender 2,500T soyoil on April 30.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on April 30 for a 2,500-tonne shipment of soyoil, company officials said on Wednesday.
The shipment would be slated for delivery in Taiwan before June 15, a company official said.
Taiwan's edible oil producers have been cutting their soybean imports and turning to soyoil imports as a result of the island's recent hog foot and mouth epidemic.

Since the epidemic was made public on March 20, a mass slaughter of nearly three million hogs has caused a significant drop in the island's demand for soymeal feed, forcing edible oil producers to cut soybean crushing to trim soymeal inventories.
Soyoil production has also fallen as the crush rate has been reduced, forcing producers to turn to crude soyoil imports to make up for the shortfall.
Soybean crushing yields two main products, oil and soymeal. Crushing to produce oil would result in a fast-growing surplus of meal for which there is no demand, crushers explained.
